newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - only prepared nations should join EMU.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - only prepared nations should join EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Friday that Europe's monetary union needed to be restricted to nations with the right economic and price policies.

"It will extremely important for the euro area to restrict entry to those countries which are ready in terms of their economic and anti-inflation policies," Tietmeyer said in a speech prepared for delivery in Copenhagen.
A copy of the speech was distributed here ahead of delivery.
Tietmeyer elaborated that the strict policy would be "to prevent a lack of anti-inflationary convergence from being transformed into real economic divergence."

Europe's currency union is scheduled to begin in 1999 with as many nations as meet the strict entry criteria. These include restrictions on budget deficits and debt, foreign exchange rates, inflation rates and long-term interest rates.
Tietmeyer also said that it was important to have a precise definition of the stability pact agreed in Dublin last December when the details are set down in legal texts over the next few weeks.
"What will be absolutely crucial at this juncture is for the requirements laid down in Dublin to be spelled out in precise terms. Failing this there might easily be unnecessary conflict later on."

Turning to Denmark's decision not to participate in the third stage of monetary union for the time being, Tietmeyer said, "naturally we in Germany respect Denmark's sovereign decision, even if we at the Bundesbank are not unreservedly happy about that decision."
"That is because it is precisely in the initial phase that we shall need stable partners in EMU."

Tietmeyer added that the door was still open for Denmark to take part in EMU at a later stage. "What has not happened yet can of course take place at some point in the future. It goes without saying, however that this is a matter for the Danes themselves to decide."

Tietmeyer also said it was likely that the Danish krone would belong to the exchange rate mechanism of EMS II from the outset of currency union, which would imply the existence of close bilateral links between the currency and Europe's common currency, the euro.
